bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable Hunspell snapshot reproduced here, the exact 8209-byte witness is split by `affdicfuzzer` into a 45-byte query word, a 4081-byte `.aff` file, and a 4082-byte `.dic` file. The malformed `.aff` half still prefix-matches several compound directives: line 2 begins with `COMPOUNDFLAG` and materializes a non-null compound flag, line 36 is `SET! UTF-8` and enables UTF-8 mode, line 47 begins with `COMPOUNDFORBIDFLAG` and materializes a non-null forbid flag, and line 49 begins with `CHECKCOMPOUNDPATTERN` while the first consumed table row at line 50 stores a 56-byte `pattern`, a 3-byte `pattern2`, a one-byte `pattern3 = "\xff"`, and sets `simplifiedcpd = 1`. This partially parsed compound state survives later affix errors because `AffixMgr::AffixMgr` only warns on `parse_file()` failure and keeps the live fields it already populated. The saved crash stack shows `HunspellImpl::checkword()` reaching the 3-or-more-word fallback call `compound_check(..., info)` at line 908 and then recursing through repeated `compound_check(...):2092` suffix calls. Inside a crashing recursive `compound_check()` call, a simplified compound-pattern pass rewrites `st`, saves `oldlen/oldcmin/oldcmax`, and increases `len` by 58 before recomputing a larger `cmax = len - cpdmin + 1`. The only in-loop site that restores those pre-rewrite scan bounds is the footer at lines 2153-2158. The staged fix shows that a `compoundforbidflag`-triggered early `continue` inside the same simplified-compound loop can bypass that footer; the exact malformed `.dic` entry that caused that path is not recoverable from the saved static artifacts, but the observed stale-bound crash shows the restore did not run before a later iteration reused the rewritten `cmax` against the current `st` buffer. Because UTF-8 mode is enabled, the continuation-byte probe `for (; (st[i] & 0xc0) == 0x80; i++)` dereferences `st[i]` before the following `if (i >= cmax) return NULL;` bailout can run, so the stale bound lets that probe read past the live `st` string. AddressSanitizer accordingly reports a `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/hunspell/affixmgr.cxx:1612`. The staged fix resolves this exact stale-bound path by restoring `cmin` and `cmax` on the early-continue path before the next simplified-compound iteration.

source.description: First scored project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant state. While reading the attacker-controlled `.aff` slice, this call consumes the earliest newline-delimited line whose first 12 bytes match `COMPOUNDFLAG` and decodes a non-null `compoundflag`, enabling the compound-word parser later reached by `checkword()`.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness is the 8209-byte file `gt_results/arvo_60034/poc` with sha256 `9afc2008aa878b552044ef119e3b8eef3b3a97f6054249f04c11144269d821a4`. `affdicfuzzer` interprets byte 0 as `wordlen = 0x2d`, materializes bytes 1..45 as the query word, and splits the remaining 8163 bytes into `/tmp/test.aff` (4081 bytes) and `/tmp/test.dic` (4082 bytes). The first relevant affix line begins with the 12-byte prefix `COMPOUNDFLAG`, so this statement is the first project-code point that turns the witness into compound-parser state used by the vulnerable path.
source.note: The malformed line is not valid affix text, but `parse_file()` only prefix-compares directive names, so `COMPOUNDFLAG...` is still accepted far enough to populate `compoundflag` before later parse errors are logged.

tainted_value_origin.description: This simplified compound-pattern rewrite derives the attacker-controlled bound that later becomes stale. The first live row parsed from aff line 50 has `pattern.size() == 56`, `pattern2.size() == 3`, and `pattern3.size() == 1`, so each application adds 58 to `len`; `setcminmax()` and `cmax = len - cpdmin + 1` then recompute a larger candidate-scan window than the original word stored in the current `st` buffer.

root_cause.description: Missing restoration root cause. After a simplified compound-pattern rewrite, this footer should restore the pre-rewrite `cmin` and `cmax` before later iterations. On the crashing path those stores are skipped, so later scans keep the larger rewritten bound against the current `st` buffer.
root_cause.note: The staged fix adds these same restoration stores on the earlier `compoundforbidflag` early-continue path, which is the only simplified-compound exit that can bypass the footer after the step-9 rewrite. Because the malformed `.dic` does not statically identify the exact forbid-flagged stem, the GT anchors root cause at the skipped restore rather than a specific `lookup()` hit.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. With UTF-8 mode enabled and stale `cmax` extending beyond the live `st` string, this continuation-byte probe dereferences `st[i]` before the following `if (i >= cmax) return NULL;` bailout can run.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports a `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of a 240-byte region allocated by `std::string::operator=`; that matches the current-call `st.assign(word)` buffer used here.

parser_admitted.description: Stack-observed admission into the vulnerable parser path. After the earlier 2-word compound attempt fails and `SPELL_COMPOUND_2` is clear, `checkword()` enters the 3-or-more-word `compound_check()` path on the attacker-controlled word under the compound state created from the malformed `.aff` file.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged workspace commit `ddec95be6412f2fe41eec33b299f4b2d5babbd0c`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `1be974933b09b5512c3656bd6f03bf31ddaf1b87`; this GT is therefore anchored to the staged snapshot that actually reproduced the saved crash.

The malformed `.dic` half does not let static inspection identify the exact text row or affixed form that made the rewritten-prefix `lookup()` take the `compoundforbidflag` early-continue path. The trace therefore anchors the bug at the skipped restoration of `cmin` and `cmax`, which the saved crash and staged fix both require, rather than guessing a specific dictionary line or `rv`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness splits the exact 8209-byte witness into a 45-byte query word plus 4081-byte `.aff` and 4082-byte `.dic` files, then constructs a `Hunspell` instance from those attacker-controlled files.

Affix parsing prefix-matches malformed lines into live compound state: it materializes `compoundflag`, enables `utf8`, materializes `compoundforbidflag`, and leaves `simplifiedcpd` plus a non-empty `checkcpdtable` entry resident even though the affix file later reports parse failure.
After direct checks fail, `checkword()` reaches the stack-observed 3-or-more-word fallback call to `compound_check()` and begins recursive compound splitting on the attacker-controlled word.

A simplified compound-pattern pass rewrites the candidate string and enlarges `len`/`cmax`; the only footer that restores those pre-rewrite bounds can be bypassed on the fix-targeted early-continue path, leaving stale scan bounds live for later iterations.

A later outer-loop iteration in the crashing recursive `compound_check()` call reuses stale `cmax`, and the UTF-8 continuation-byte probe reads past the live `st` string before the following `i >= cmax` bailout.

fine_trace.note: Harness-only step. Byte 0 of the exact staged witness is `0x2d`, so `affdicfuzzer` materializes a 45-byte query word, a 4081-byte `/tmp/test.aff`, and a 4082-byte `/tmp/test.dic` from the 8209-byte blob.

Source. The earliest relevant affix line begins with the 12-byte prefix `COMPOUNDFLAG`, so this call consumes that malformed line and decodes a non-null `compoundflag`. That makes `AffixMgr::get_compound()` true later even though the remainder of the line is malformed affix text.

The `.aff` slice's line 36 is exactly `SET! UTF-8`. It still passes the 3-byte directive prefix check `SET`, so `parse_string()` stores `UTF-8` and this branch enables UTF-8 mode. That flag selects the `st[i]` continuation-byte probe at the eventual sink.

The `.aff` slice's line 47 begins with the 18-byte prefix `COMPOUNDFORBIDFLAG` and its second whitespace-delimited token is `4`, so this call materializes a non-null `compoundforbidflag` used by the fix-targeted early-continue path in `compound_check()`.

The malformed affix slice also reaches `parse_checkcpdtable()`: line 49 begins with `CHECKCOMPOUNDPATTERN` and its second token starts with `5`, so Hunspell expects five pattern rows. The first consumed row at line 50 reaches cases 1-3 here, storing a 56-byte `pattern`, a 3-byte `pattern2`, and a one-byte `pattern3 = "\xff"` into `checkcpdtable`, then setting `simplifiedcpd = 1`. Even if later table rows are corrupt, `AffixMgr::AffixMgr` only warns on `parse_file()` failure, so this partially parsed entry remains live.

After the earlier 2-word compound attempt fails and `SPELL_COMPOUND_2` is clear, `checkword()` makes the 3-or-more-word `compound_check()` call recorded in the ASAN stack. This feeds the attacker-controlled word into the vulnerable compound splitter under the compound-enabled state from step 2.

At entry to the crashing `compound_check()` call, `setcminmax()` derives the original split window `[cmin, cmax)` from the current recursive word length and `cpdmin`. These are the baseline bounds that the later restore is supposed to recover.

The current recursive word is copied into heap-backed `st`, the string object later read at the sink. The saved ASAN allocation report attributes the faulting region to `std::string::operator=`, which is consistent with this assignment.

fine_trace.var: st, i, soldi, len, oldcmin, oldcmax, cmin, cmax
fine_trace.note: When a simplified-compound retry reaches an offset where the step-5 row's one-byte `pattern3 = "\xff"` matches, this block rewrites `st`, records `soldi` plus the pre-rewrite bounds in `oldcmin` and `oldcmax`, adds 58 to `len`, and recomputes `cmin` and `cmax` for the rewritten candidate. On the crashing path this is the step that creates the enlarged `cmax` later left stale.

After the step-9 rewrite, `compound_check()` saves the byte at the current split point and temporarily truncates `st` there. That mutation defines the exact prefix string passed to `lookup(st.c_str(), i)`; the saved malformed `.dic` does not let static inspection name the specific matching entry, but this is the source-level prefix state whose early exit determines whether the step-9 bounds get restored.

fine_trace.var: soldi, len, cmin, cmax, oldlen, oldcmin, oldcmax
fine_trace.note: Root cause. After a simplified-pattern rewrite sets `soldi != 0` and records `oldlen/oldcmin/oldcmax`, this footer is the only in-loop restoration site for those pre-rewrite bounds. The staged fix adds equivalent `cmin = oldcmin; cmax = oldcmax;` stores on the earlier `compoundforbidflag` early-continue path, showing that the vulnerable path can reach the next simplified pass without executing this block. Because the malformed `.dic` does not statically isolate the exact forbid-flagged stem, the trace anchors the bug at this skipped restoration site rather than naming a specific `rv`.

depends_on.via: soldi, oldlen, oldcmin, oldcmax, len, cmin, cmax

fine_trace.note: Because step 11's restore does not run on the buggy path, the crashing recursive call later resumes its outer split scan with the step-9 `cmax` still reflecting the rewritten candidate rather than the current `st` size. The repeated `compound_check(...):2092` frames in the saved stack are collapsed here: each recursive suffix call reuses the same state machine, and in the final crashing call this stale loop guard keeps iterating over a range wider than the live `st` buffer.

Sink. Because step 3 enabled UTF-8 mode, this continuation-byte probe reads `st[i]` before the following `if (i >= cmax) return NULL;` bailout can run. With step 12's stale `cmax`, the probe can dereference past the live `st` heap string. AddressSanitizer reports this line as a `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1`, 0 bytes to the right of a 240-byte region.

format.name: affdicfuzzer split word/aff/dic blob
format.contract: Exactly the 8209-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_60034/poc` (sha256 `9afc2008aa878b552044ef119e3b8eef3b3a97f6054249f04c11144269d821a4`). Byte 0 is `0x2d`, so the next 45 bytes become the query word and the remaining 8163 bytes split into a 4081-byte `.aff` file and a 4082-byte `.dic` file. The crash-relevant property of this exact witness is that the `.aff` half still prefix-matches into `COMPOUNDFLAG`, `SET`, `COMPOUNDFORBIDFLAG`, and `CHECKCOMPOUNDPATTERN` parsing, leaving compound parsing enabled, UTF-8 mode enabled, a non-null forbid flag, and a non-empty simplified compound-pattern entry live despite later parse failure. Stage 01's saved run then reaches the 3-or-more-word `compound_check()` path and eventually reuses stale `cmin` and `cmax` until the UTF-8 continuation-byte probe reads `st[i]` one byte past the current heap string.
